## Functions

```{r}
plot_interval <- function(data, var, trim = 0.99,
                          xlab = "days", ylab = "cases") {
  x <- dplyr::pull(data, {{ var }})
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]

  stats <- tibble(stat = c("mean", "median"),
                  value = c(mean(x), median(x)))

  ggplot(data, aes({{ var }})) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, boundary = -0.5,
                   fill = "grey80", colour = "white") +
    geom_vline(data = stats, aes(xintercept = value, colour = stat, linetype = stat),
               linewidth = 0.7) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(mean = "black", median = "grey40")) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c(mean = 1, median = 2)) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = quantile(x, c(0, trim))) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = ylab, colour = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
}
```

## Model

![](img/mod_res3_1.png)

```{r}
state_names <- c(
  "S_C", "E_C", "I_C_pre", "I_C_post", "R_C",
  "S_H", "E_H", "I_H_pre", "I_H_post", "Q", "R_H",
  "cum_onset_C", "cum_onset_H", "cum_noso", "cum_adm_rash", "cum_inf_C"
)

measles_ode <- function(t, y, p) {
  S_C <- y[["S_C"]]
  E_C <- y[["E_C"]]
  R_C <- y[["R_C"]]
  I_C_pre <- y[["I_C_pre"]]
  I_C_post <- y[["I_C_post"]]
  S_H <- y[["S_H"]]
  E_H <- y[["E_H"]]
  R_H <- y[["R_H"]]
  Q <- y[["Q"]]
  I_H_pre <- y[["I_H_pre"]]
  I_H_post <- y[["I_H_post"]]
  
  beta_C   <- p[["beta_C"]]
  beta_H  <- p[["beta_H"]]
  xi_alpha <- p[["xi_alpha"]]
  alpha   <- p[["alpha"]]
  p_a      <- p[["p_a"]]
  p_i     <- p[["p_i"]]
  sigma    <- p[["sigma"]]
  eta     <- p[["eta"]]
  gamma <- p[["gamma"]]
  delta    <- p[["delta"]]
  delta_M <- p[["delta_M"]]
  
  ## ---- forces of infection
  N_C     <- S_C + E_C + I_C_pre + I_C_post + R_C
  N_H_mix <- S_H + E_H + I_H_pre + I_H_post + R_H
  
  lambda_C <- beta_C * (I_C_pre + I_C_post) / N_C
  lambda_H <- if (N_H_mix > 0) beta_H * (I_H_pre + I_H_post) / N_H_mix else 0   # no hospital: no ward infections
  
  ## ---- community
  dS_C      <- -lambda_C * S_C - xi_alpha * S_C + delta * S_H
  
  dE_C      <-  lambda_C * S_C - sigma * E_C - xi_alpha * E_C + delta * E_H
  
  ## I_C_pre leaves by four routes: rash onset splits three ways, plus general
  ## admission. The three onset coefficients sum to eta.
  dI_C_pre  <-  sigma * E_C -
    (1 - p_a) * eta * I_C_pre -          # -> I_C_post
    p_a * (1 - p_i) * eta * I_C_pre -    # -> I_H_post
    p_a * p_i * eta * I_C_pre -          # -> Q
    xi_alpha * I_C_pre +                 # -> I_H_pre
    delta * I_H_pre                      # <- I_H_pre
  
  dI_C_post <-  (1 - p_a) * eta * I_C_pre -          # <- I_C_pre
    gamma * I_C_post
  
  dR_C      <-  gamma * I_C_post - alpha * R_C + delta * R_H + delta_M * Q
  
  ## ---- hospital
  dS_H      <-  xi_alpha * S_C - lambda_H * S_H - delta * S_H
  
  dE_H      <-  lambda_H * S_H + xi_alpha * E_C - sigma * E_H - delta * E_H
  
  ## I_H_pre leaves by three routes: rash onset splits two ways, plus discharge.
  ## The two onset coefficients sum to eta.
  dI_H_pre  <-  sigma * E_H +
    xi_alpha * I_C_pre -                 # <- I_C_pre
    (1 - p_i) * eta * I_H_pre -          # -> I_H_post
    p_i * eta * I_H_pre -                # -> Q
    delta * I_H_pre                      # -> I_C_pre
  
  dI_H_post <-  (1 - p_i) * eta * I_H_pre +          # <- I_H_pre
    p_a * (1 - p_i) * eta * I_C_pre -    # <- I_C_pre
    gamma * I_H_post
  
  dQ        <-  p_i * eta * I_H_pre +                # <- I_H_pre
    p_a * p_i * eta * I_C_pre -          # <- I_C_pre
    delta_M * Q
  
  dR_H      <-  gamma * I_H_post + alpha * R_C - delta * R_H
  
  ## ---- cumulative trackers -------------------------------------------------
  dcum_onset_C  <- eta * I_C_pre          # all community rash onsets
  dcum_onset_H  <- eta * I_H_pre          # admissions, rash appeared AFTER arrival
  dcum_noso     <- lambda_H * S_H         # infections acquired as an inpatient
  dcum_adm_rash <- p_a * eta * I_C_pre    # admissions, rash present on arrival
  dcum_inf_C    <- lambda_C * S_C         # infections acquired in the community
  
  ## names are documentation: deSolve reads this by position, so the order must
  ## match state_names. The check below enforces that.
  list(
    c(
      S_C = dS_C,
      E_C = dE_C,
      I_C_pre = dI_C_pre,
      I_C_post = dI_C_post,
      R_C = dR_C,
      S_H = dS_H,
      E_H = dE_H,
      I_H_pre = dI_H_pre,
      I_H_post = dI_H_post,
      Q = dQ,
      R_H = dR_H,
      cum_onset_C = dcum_onset_C,
      cum_onset_H = dcum_onset_H,
      cum_noso = dcum_noso,
      cum_adm_rash = dcum_adm_rash,
      cum_inf_C = dcum_inf_C
    )
  )
}
```

Helpers.

`p_i` is fixed rather than estimated: it only changes how long `I_H_post` transmits, which the case series barely sees. It is varied in a sensitivity analysis instead.

```{r}
p_i_fixed <- 0.9

## s_C0 and s_H0 are fixed inputs, set in the Parameters section. seed is the
## number of latent infections in the community at t = 0.
init_state <- function(seed) {
  y <- c(
    S_C = s_C0 * N_C0 - seed, E_C = seed,
    I_C_pre = 0, I_C_post = 0, R_C = (1 - s_C0) * N_C0,
    S_H = s_H0 * N_H0, E_H = 0, I_H_pre = 0, I_H_post = 0, Q = 0,
    R_H = (1 - s_H0) * N_H0,
    cum_onset_C = 0, cum_onset_H = 0, cum_noso = 0,
    cum_adm_rash = 0, cum_inf_C = 0
  )
  y[state_names]
}

## ODE parameters from the fitted parameters. xi_alpha and alpha depend only on
## the fixed s_C0 and s_H0, so they are computed once, in the Parameters section.
make_params <- function(par) {
  c(beta_C = par[["beta_C"]], beta_H = par[["kappa"]] * par[["beta_C"]],
    xi_alpha = xi_alpha, alpha = alpha,
    p_a = par[["p_a"]],
    p_i = if ("p_i" %in% names(par)) par[["p_i"]] else p_i_fixed,
    delta = delta, delta_M = delta_M,
    sigma = sigma, eta = eta, gamma = gamma)
}

solve_model <- function(par, times) {
  out <- tryCatch(
    ode(y = init_state(par[["seed"]]),
        times = times, func = measles_ode,
        parms = make_params(par),
        method = "lsoda", atol = 1e-3, rtol = 1e-6),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(out) || nrow(out) != length(times) || anyNA(out)) return(NULL)
  out
}

## weekly quantities. The two case types partition all rash onsets:
##   adm_w  = p_a * onset_C + onset_H   children admitted with measles
##   out_w  = (1 - p_a) * onset_C       community cases not admitted
run_model <- function(par, n_weeks, full = FALSE) {

  sol <- solve_model(par, seq.int(0L, n_weeks * 7L, by = 7L))
  if (is.null(sol)) return(NULL)

  onset_C  <- diff(sol[, "cum_onset_C"])
  onset_H  <- diff(sol[, "cum_onset_H"])
  adm_rash <- diff(sol[, "cum_adm_rash"])

  if (!full) {
    return(list(adm = adm_rash + onset_H,
                out = onset_C - adm_rash))
  }

  keep <- -1L   # drop t = 0, so each row pairs with one diff()

  tibble(
    week     = seq_len(n_weeks),
    onset_C  = onset_C,
    onset_H  = onset_H,
    adm      = adm_rash + onset_H,
    out      = onset_C - adm_rash,
    noso     = diff(sol[, "cum_noso"]),
    inf_C    = diff(sol[, "cum_inf_C"]),
    I_H_pre  = sol[keep, "I_H_pre"],
    I_H_post = sol[keep, "I_H_post"],
    Q        = sol[keep, "Q"],
    N_H      = rowSums(sol[keep, c("S_H", "E_H", "I_H_pre",
                                   "I_H_post", "Q", "R_H")])
  )
}
```

## Parameters

Disease natural history (rate per day):

```{r}
sigma <- 1 / 8      # exposed -> infectious
eta   <- 1 / 4      # pre-rash -> post-rash
gamma <- 1 / 4      # post-rash -> removed
```

### Hospital population and alpha_bar

Number of children 15 years and under in HCMC:

```{r}
N <- df_census |>
  filter(age <= 15) |>
  pull(n) |>
  sum()

cat("Total population N:", N)
```

Children's Hospital 1 reported 90,000 admissions per year. Assume HCMC total is
5 times CH1, of which 40% are HCMC residents. Mean length of stay 5.2 days.

`alpha_bar` is admissions per **community** child per day, because in the ODE
the admission flows multiply community compartments. Working from the admission
count avoids needing `N_C0` before `alpha_bar` is known, and makes the
disease-free state balance exactly.

```{r}
resident_frac <- 0.4
delta         <- 1 / 5.2

adm_per_day <- 5 * resident_frac * 90000 / 365
N_H0        <- adm_per_day / delta
N_C0        <- N - N_H0
alpha_bar   <- adm_per_day / N_C0

s_C0 <- 0.08
s_H0 <- 0.29
xi       <- (s_H0 * (1 - s_C0)) / (s_C0 * (1 - s_H0))
alpha    <- alpha_bar / (1 + s_C0 * (xi - 1))
xi_alpha <- xi * alpha
```

### p_a and the instantaneous-admission assumption

The model admits a fraction `p_a` of community cases **at rash onset**, with no
delay. That is justified only if the observed onset-to-admission interval is
short. HCMC records a median of 0 days; the Hanoi line list is shown here for
comparison.

```{r}
d <- df_hn |>
  mutate(ad_delay = as.numeric(admission_date - onset_date)) |>
  filter(!is.na(ad_delay), ad_delay >= 0, ad_delay <= 10,
         source_province == "community", province == "Ha Noi")

d |> summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(ad_delay), median = median(ad_delay))

plot_interval(d, ad_delay, trim = 0.99,
              xlab = "onset to admission delay (days)", ylab = "cases")
```

### delta_M

Discharge rate from isolation, from measles length of stay at Children's Hospital 2.

```{r}
d <- df_ch2 |>
  mutate(stay = as.numeric(discharge - admission)) |>
  filter(!is.na(stay), stay >= 0, stay < 30)

est <- d |> summarise(n = n(), los_M = mean(stay), median = median(stay))
est

plot_interval(d, stay, xlab = "length of stay (days)", ylab = "cases")

delta_M <- 1 / est$los_M
cat("delta_M:", round(delta_M, 4), " mean isolated stay:",
    round(1 / delta_M, 1), "days\n")
```

### Structural check

Confirms the derivative vector comes back in the order `state_names` expects
and that the population is conserved. It has to run after the constants above,
because `make_params` and `init_state` read them.

```{r}
local({
  par <- c(beta_C = 2.2, kappa = 0.5, p_a = 0.1, seed = 10)
  d   <- measles_ode(0, init_state(10), make_params(par))[[1]]
  stopifnot(identical(names(d), state_names))
  stopifnot(abs(sum(d)) < 1e-6)
  cat("model check: state order and conservation OK\n")
})
```

## Disease-free equilibrium check

With transmission switched off, hospital occupancy and hospital susceptibility
must stay flat. Drift means the inputs are inconsistent and every fit inherits
an artificial transient.

```{r}
disease_free <- function(days = 365) {

  p <- make_params(c(beta_C = 0, kappa = 0, p_a = 0.1))   # no transmission

  ode(y = init_state(0), times = 0:days,
      func = measles_ode, parms = p,
      method = "lsoda", atol = 1e-3, rtol = 1e-6) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(
      day = time,
      N_H = S_H + E_H + I_H_pre + I_H_post + Q + R_H,
      s_H = S_H / (S_H + E_H + I_H_pre + I_H_post + R_H),
      s_C = S_C / (S_C + E_C + I_C_pre + I_C_post + R_C)
    )
}

df_check <- disease_free()

df_check |>
  summarise(N_H_drift_pct = 100 * (last(N_H) / first(N_H) - 1),
            s_H_drift_pct = 100 * (last(s_H) / first(s_H) - 1),
            s_C_drift_pct = 100 * (last(s_C) / first(s_C) - 1))

df_check |>
  ggplot(aes(day, N_H)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = N_H0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  labs(x = "Day", y = "Hospital population N_H",
       subtitle = "Dashed line is the specified N_H(0)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11)
```

## Calibration

### Options

The three fits to compare are:

- total cases, as before: `obs_model = "total"`, `fit_rho = TRUE`
- no under-reporting: `fit_rho = FALSE`
- inpatients and outpatients separately: `obs_model = "split"`

```{r}
obs_model <- "total"   # "total": one negative binomial on all weekly cases
                       # "split": one each for inpatients and outpatients
fit_rho   <- T      # TRUE: estimate the reporting fraction rho
                       # FALSE: no under-reporting, rho fixed at 1

stopifnot(obs_model %in% c("total", "split"), is.logical(fit_rho))

## fitted parameters for these options
par_names <- c("beta_C", "kappa", "p_a", "seed",
               if (fit_rho) "rho",
               if (obs_model == "total") "phi" else c("phi_in", "phi_out"))
par_names

## one file per option, so the fits can be compared later
fit_file <- sprintf("measles_fit_%s_rho%s_sC%s.rds", obs_model, fit_rho, s_C0)
```

Epidemic curve by inpatient and outpatient:

```{r}
df_week_wide <- df_hcmc |>
  filter(age <= 15) |>
  mutate(
    date = as_date(ngay_nv),
    week = floor_date(date, "week", week_start = 1),
    type = if_else(inpatient, "inpatient", "outpatient")
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(week), !is.na(type)) |>
  count(week, type, name = "cases") |>
  complete(week = seq(min(week), max(week), by = "week"), type,
           fill = list(cases = 0)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = cases, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(total = inpatient + outpatient,
         prop_inpatient = inpatient / total) |>
  arrange(week)

n_lead_weeks <- 8      # simulated weeks before the first observed week

obs <- df_week_wide |>
  arrange(week) |>
  mutate(t_week = row_number() + n_lead_weeks)

n_weeks   <- max(obs$t_week)
obs_idx   <- obs$t_week
obs_total <- obs$total
obs_in    <- obs$inpatient
obs_out   <- obs$outpatient
t0_date   <- min(obs$week) - 7 * (n_lead_weeks + 1)

n_total <- as.integer(sum(obs$total))
n_in    <- as.integer(sum(obs$inpatient))

cat("weeks:", n_weeks, " total:", n_total, " inpatient:", n_in,
    " share:", round(n_in / n_total, 3), "\n")
```

### Likelihood

Weekly reported cases follow a negative binomial distribution, with mean `rho` times the model's weekly rash onsets. The options above decide how the model meets the data:

- `obs_model = "total"`: one negative binomial for all weekly cases, with mean
  `rho * (adm + out)` and dispersion `phi`.
- `obs_model = "split"`: one negative binomial for inpatients, with mean `rho * adm`, and one for outpatients, with mean `rho * out`. Each has its own
  dispersion, `phi_in` and `phi_out`.
- `fit_rho = FALSE`: `rho` is fixed at 1, so every case is assumed reported.

### Prior

```{r}
## Bounds, prior density and prior sampler of every parameter that can be
## fitted. The options decide which ones are used (par_names).
priors <- list(
  beta_C = list(lower = 0.1, upper = 20,
                d = \(x) dunif(x, 0.1, 20, log = TRUE),
                r = \(n) runif(n, 0.1, 20)),
  kappa  = list(lower = 0, upper = 10,
                d = \(x) dunif(x, 0, 10, log = TRUE),
                r = \(n) runif(n, 0, 10)),
  p_a    = list(lower = 0.005, upper = 0.95,      # mean 0.29, deliberately wide
                d = \(x) dbeta(x, 2, 5, log = TRUE),
                r = \(n) rbeta(n, 2, 5)),
  seed   = list(lower = 1, upper = 50,
                d = \(x) dunif(x, 1, 50, log = TRUE),
                r = \(n) runif(n, 1, 50)),
  rho    = list(lower = 0.001, upper = 1,
                d = \(x) dbeta(x, 2, 8, log = TRUE),
                r = \(n) rbeta(n, 2, 8)),
  phi    = list(lower = 0.1, upper = 100,
                d = \(x) dunif(x, 0.1, 100, log = TRUE),
                r = \(n) runif(n, 0.1, 100))
)
priors$phi_in  <- priors$phi    # split option: the same prior for each series
priors$phi_out <- priors$phi

lower <- map_dbl(priors[par_names], \(p) p$lower)
upper <- map_dbl(priors[par_names], \(p) p$upper)

## base R only (mapply, not purrr): this also runs on the parallel workers,
## which load deSolve and nothing else
log_prior <- function(x) {
  sum(mapply(\(p, v) p$d(v), priors[par_names], as.numeric(x)))
}

## draw from the prior, not from the bounding box, so the DEzs archive starts
## where the prior has weight
prior_sampler <- function(n = 1) {
  m <- sapply(priors[par_names], \(p) p$r(n))
  if (n == 1) as.numeric(m) else m
}

prior <- createPrior(density = log_prior, sampler = prior_sampler,
                     lower = lower, upper = upper)
```

### Fit

Three independent DEzs runs, each with six internal chains. The package
documentation warns that Gelman diagnostics applied to the internal chains of a
single population sampler can be optimistic, because those chains are only
argued to be independent after burn-in. `nrChains` controls independent runs and
is separate from the internal chain count.

## Posterior

```{r}
## derived quantities (thesis Section 4.3.5); s_C0, s_H0 and xi_alpha are fixed.
## One function, so the posterior draws and the MAP use the same formulas.
add_derived <- function(d) {
  d |>
    mutate(
      beta_H  = kappa * beta_C,
      D_C     = (eta + delta) / (eta + xi_alpha + delta) * (1 / eta + (1 - p_a) / gamma),
      R0C     = beta_C * D_C,             # community, everyone susceptible
      R_C_eff = s_C0 * R0C,               # community, at the start of the outbreak
      R0H     = beta_H * ((eta + xi_alpha) / (eta * (eta + xi_alpha + delta)) +
                  (1 - p_i_fixed) / gamma * (eta + xi_alpha + p_a * delta) /
                  (eta + xi_alpha + delta)),
      per_case_ratio = kappa * s_H0 / s_C0   # infections per case, H relative to C
    )
}

post <- getSample(fit, thin = 20) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  setNames(par_names) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  add_derived()

## MAP: the posterior draw with the highest log posterior (BayesianTools::MAP).
## Derived quantities are computed at this one parameter set.
best    <- MAP(fit)
map_row <- as_tibble_row(best$parametersMAP[par_names]) |> add_derived()

vars <- c("beta_C", "beta_H", "R0C", "R_C_eff", "R0H", "kappa", "p_a",
          "per_case_ratio", "seed",
          intersect(c("rho", "phi", "phi_in", "phi_out"), names(post)))

map_long <- map_row |>
  select(all_of(vars)) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "par", values_to = "MAP")

post |>
  select(all_of(vars)) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "par") |>
  group_by(par = factor(par, levels = vars)) |>
  summarise(lo = quantile(value, 0.025), hi = quantile(value, 0.975)) |>
  mutate(par = as.character(par)) |>
  left_join(map_long, by = "par") |>
  relocate(MAP, .after = par) |>
  mutate(crI = paste0(sprintf("%.2f", lo), "-", sprintf("%.2f", hi))) |>
  # write.csv("post.csv", quote = F, row.names = F)
  print(n = Inf)
```

### Prediction vs observation

```{r}
set.seed(20260921)
wk2date <- function(w) t0_date + 7 * w

## posterior predictive draws. y_rep is the weekly total; in the split option it
## is the sum of the inpatient and outpatient draws.
pp <- post |>
  slice_sample(n = 500) |>
  mutate(draw = row_number()) |>
  group_split(draw) |>
  map_dfr(function(d) {
    par <- unlist(d[par_names])
    s <- run_model(par, n_weeks, full = TRUE)
    if (is.null(s)) return(NULL)
    rho <- if (fit_rho) d$rho else 1

    res <- tibble(draw   = d$draw,
                  week   = s$week,
                  mu_in  = rho * s$adm,
                  mu_out = rho * s$out,
                  mu     = mu_in + mu_out,
                  share  = s$adm / (s$adm + s$out),
                  noso   = s$noso)

    if (obs_model == "total") {
      res |> mutate(y_rep = rnbinom(n(), mu = mu, size = d$phi))
    } else {
      res |> mutate(y_in  = rnbinom(n(), mu = mu_in,  size = d$phi_in),
                    y_out = rnbinom(n(), mu = mu_out, size = d$phi_out),
                    y_rep = y_in + y_out)
    }
  })

band <- pp |>
  group_by(week) |>
  summarise(med      = median(mu),
            lo95     = quantile(y_rep, 0.025), hi95 = quantile(y_rep, 0.975),
            lo50     = quantile(y_rep, 0.25),  hi50 = quantile(y_rep, 0.75),
            mean_rep = mean(y_rep), sd_rep = sd(y_rep),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(date = wk2date(week))

obs_d <- obs |> mutate(date = wk2date(t_week))
```

```{r}
         rho = "rho", phi = "phi", phi_in = "phi['in']", phi_out = "phi['out']")

## the campaign is not in the model; shading it shows where the model may depart

campaign_layer <- geom_rect(

# =============================================================================
# Fit

fig_fit <- ggplot(band, aes(date)) +
  campaign_layer +
  annotate("text", x = campaign$start, y = Inf, label = "Vaccination campaign",
           hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.6, size = 3, colour = "grey35") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo95, ymax = hi95), fill = "grey82") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo50, ymax = hi50), fill = "grey62") +

             shape = 21, fill = "white", size = 1.5, stroke = 0.5) +

  labs(x = NULL, y = "Weekly cases") +
  theme_thesis


# =============================================================================
# Residuals
#
# Pearson residuals from the posterior predictive draws: observed minus the
# predictive mean, divided by the predictive SD. This works for every option.
# Runs of same-signed residuals mean structure the model does not capture.
# =============================================================================

resid_df <- obs_d |>
  left_join(band |> select(week, mean_rep, sd_rep), by = c("t_week" = "week")) |>
  mutate(resid = (total - mean_rep) / sd_rep)

fig_resid <- ggplot(resid_df, aes(date, resid)) +
  campaign_layer +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-2, 2), linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, fill = "white", size = 1.3, stroke = 0.5) +
  date_axis +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(-2, 0, 2)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Residual") +
  theme_thesis


# =============================================================================
# Posterior distributions and correlations
#
# Diagonal: posterior and prior densities, both scaled by the posterior's peak,
# so a prior that the data overrode reads as flat. Lower triangle: 2,000 joint
# draws, minus the few outside the axis range. Upper triangle: posterior
# correlation.
# =============================================================================

post_p  <- post |> select(all_of(par_names))
prior_p <- prior_sampler(20000) |> as.data.frame() |> setNames(par_names)

## axis range per parameter: the central 99% of the posterior
lo  <- map_dbl(post_p, ~ quantile(.x, 0.005))
hi  <- map_dbl(post_p, ~ quantile(.x, 0.995))
mid <- (lo + hi) / 2

cells <- expand_grid(xvar = par_names, yvar = par_names) |>
  mutate(i = match(yvar, par_names), j = match(xvar, par_names))

as_panel <- function(d) {
  d |> mutate(xvar = factor(xvar, levels = par_names),
              yvar = factor(yvar, levels = par_names))
}

thin <- post_p |> slice_sample(n = 2000)

## a draw outside the range would stretch its row or column, so drop it
pts <- cells |>
  filter(i > j) |>
  mutate(xy = map2(xvar, yvar, ~ tibble(x = thin[[.x]], y = thin[[.y]]))) |>
  unnest(xy) |>
  filter(x >= lo[xvar], x <= hi[xvar], y >= lo[yvar], y <= hi[yvar]) |>
  as_panel()

dens <- map_dfr(par_names, function(p) {
  d_post <- density(post_p[[p]],  from = lo[[p]], to = hi[[p]], n = 200)
  d_pri  <- density(prior_p[[p]], from = lo[[p]], to = hi[[p]], n = 200)
  k <- 0.95 * (hi[[p]] - lo[[p]]) / max(d_post$y)
  bind_rows(tibble(dist = "Posterior", x = d_post$x, y = lo[[p]] + k * d_post$y),
            tibble(dist = "Prior",     x = d_pri$x,  y = lo[[p]] + k * d_pri$y)) |>
    mutate(xvar = p, yvar = p)
}) |>
  as_panel()

cors <- cells |>
  filter(i < j) |>
  mutate(r = map2_dbl(xvar, yvar, ~ cor(post_p[[.x]], post_p[[.y]])),
         x = mid[xvar], y = mid[yvar]) |>
  as_panel()

## at most two ticks per axis, away from the panel edges. If the two ticks are
## closer than 45% of the range, their labels can touch, so keep only the tick
## nearer the middle.
two_breaks <- function(l) {
  b <- pretty(l, n = 4)
  b <- b[b > l[1] + 0.1 * diff(l) & b < l[2] - 0.1 * diff(l)]
  if (length(b) > 2) b <- b[c(1, length(b))]
  if (length(b) == 2 && diff(b) < 0.45 * diff(l)) b <- b[which.min(abs(b - mean(l)))]
  b
}

## hold every row and column to its parameter's range
limits <- bind_rows(
  cells |> transmute(xvar, yvar, x = lo[xvar], y = lo[yvar]),
  cells |> transmute(xvar, yvar, x = hi[xvar], y = hi[yvar])
) |>
  as_panel()

fig_corner <- ggplot() +
  geom_blank(data = limits, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_rect(data = cors, aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
                             fill = r)) +
  geom_text(data = cors, aes(x, y, label = sprintf("%.2f", r),
                             colour = abs(r) > 0.6), size = 2.6) +
  geom_point(data = pts, aes(x, y), size = 0.2, alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(data = dens, aes(x, y, linetype = dist), linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_grid(yvar ~ xvar, scales = "free", switch = "both",
             labeller = as_labeller(lbl, default = label_parsed)) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B",
                       limits = c(-1, 1), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "black", `TRUE` = "white"),
                      guide = "none") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(Posterior = "solid", Prior = "dashed"),
                        name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = two_breaks,
                     guide = guide_axis(check.overlap = TRUE)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = two_breaks,
                     guide = guide_axis(check.overlap = TRUE)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_thesis +
  theme(aspect.ratio      = 1,                        # square cells
        strip.placement   = "outside",
        strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0),  # horizontal row labels
        panel.border      = element_rect(colour = "grey75", fill = NA),
        axis.line         = element_blank(),
        axis.text         = element_text(size = 6),
        panel.spacing     = unit(1.2, "mm"),
        legend.position   = "right")                  # the empty space on the right


# =============================================================================
# Rank plots, one line per independent run, with R-hat and ESS
#
# Each run's six internal chains are pooled, so the plot compares the three
# independent runs. Draws come from each run separately, so the grouping does
# not depend on how getSample() orders chains in the combined object.
# =============================================================================

by_run <- map_dfr(seq_along(fit), function(i) {
  getSample(fit[[i]]) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    setNames(par_names) |>
    mutate(run = factor(i))
})

stopifnot(nrow(by_run) == nrow(getSample(fit)))   # same draws as elsewhere

n_bins     <- 20
rank_break <- seq(0, nrow(by_run), length.out = n_bins + 1)   # equal-count bins
expected   <- nrow(by_run) / nlevels(by_run$run) / n_bins     # per bin if uniform

rank_df <- by_run |>
  pivot_longer(-run, names_to = "parameter") |>
  mutate(parameter = factor(parameter, levels = par_names)) |>
  group_by(parameter) |>
  mutate(rank = rank(value)) |>
  ungroup()

## rank-normalised R-hat and the smaller of bulk and tail ESS, per parameter
conv <- posterior::summarise_draws(draws, "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail") |>
  filter(variable %in% par_names) |>
  transmute(parameter = factor(variable, levels = par_names),
            x = nrow(by_run) / 2,
            label = sprintf("R-hat %.2f\nESS %s", rhat,
                            format(round(pmin(ess_bulk, ess_tail)),
                                   big.mark = ",")))

fig_rank <- ggplot(rank_df, aes(rank, colour = run)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = expected, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  stat_bin(geom = "line", breaks = rank_break, pad = FALSE,
           position = "identity", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(data = conv, aes(x, 0, label = label), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            vjust = -0.4, size = 2.2, colour = "grey30") +
  facet_wrap(~ parameter, nrow = 1,                  # one row saves height
             labeller = as_labeller(lbl, default = label_parsed)) +
  ggsci::scale_colour_nejm(guide = "none") +   # lines are runs; see caption
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), n.breaks = 3) +
  labs(x = "Rank of draw, pooled across runs", y = "Draws per bin") +
  theme_thesis +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7))


# =============================================================================
# One figure
#
# wrap_elements() places C as one image. Without it, patchwork lines up C's
# outside row labels with the axes of A, B and D, and that leaves a gap between
# their axes and their plots.
# =============================================================================

fig_all <-
  (fig_fit + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
                   axis.ticks.x = element_blank())) /
  fig_resid /
  wrap_elements(full = fig_corner) /
  fig_rank +
  plot_layout(heights = c(4.5, 1.8, 15, 2.2)) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12))

fig_all
```

### Values calibration

```{r, eval=FALSE}
fmt <- function(x, d = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")

## point estimate `at` (the MAP) and the 95% CrI of the draws `x`
est_ci <- function(x, at, d = 2) sprintf("%s (%s to %s)", fmt(at, d),
                                         fmt(quantile(x, 0.025), d),
                                         fmt(quantile(x, 0.975), d))

## 1. weekly counts inside the 95% posterior predictive interval
cov <- obs |>
  left_join(band |> select(week, lo95, hi95), by = c("t_week" = "week")) |>
  summarise(n_in_band = sum(total >= lo95 & total <= hi95),
            n_weeks   = n(),
            pct       = 100 * n_in_band / n_weeks)

## 2. fitted totals per draw, over observed weeks only (lead weeks excluded).
## rho cancels in the share, so it is the model's share of admitted cases.
tot <- pp |>
  filter(week %in% obs_idx) |>
  group_by(draw) |>
  summarise(rep_total = sum(mu),
            share     = sum(mu_in) / sum(mu_in + mu_out),
            .groups   = "drop")

## the same two totals at the MAP (Posterior section)
sim_map <- run_model(best$parametersMAP, n_weeks)
rho_map <- if (fit_rho) best$parametersMAP[["rho"]] else 1
map_tot <- c(rep_total = rho_map * sum(sim_map$adm[obs_idx] + sim_map$out[obs_idx]),
             share     = sum(sim_map$adm[obs_idx]) /
                         sum(sim_map$adm[obs_idx] + sim_map$out[obs_idx]))

## 3. parameter estimates and contraction relative to the prior
prior_draws <- prior_sampler(20000) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  setNames(par_names) |>
  as_tibble()

par_tab <- tibble(parameter = par_names) |>
  mutate(estimate    = map_chr(parameter, ~ est_ci(post[[.x]], map_row[[.x]], 3)),
         contraction = map_dbl(parameter,
                               ~ 1 - var(post[[.x]]) / var(prior_draws[[.x]])))

cov
tot |> summarise(rep_total = est_ci(rep_total, map_tot[["rep_total"]], 0),
                 share     = est_ci(share, map_tot[["share"]], 3))
print(par_tab, n = Inf)

## the paragraph, filled in
rho_txt <- if (fit_rho) est_ci(post$rho, map_row$rho) else "fixed at 1"

cat(sprintf(paste0(
  "%d of %d weekly counts (%.0f%%) fell inside the 95%% posterior predictive ",
  "interval. Values are MAP (95%% CrI). The model gave %s reported cases against ",
  "%s observed, and an inpatient share of %s against %s observed; both were ",
  "fitted. The community effective reproduction number was %s, p_a %s and ",
  "rho %s, with s_C0 and s_H0 fixed at %s and %s. kappa was %s, conditional ",
  "on p_i = %s.\n"),
  cov$n_in_band, cov$n_weeks, cov$pct,
  est_ci(tot$rep_total, map_tot[["rep_total"]], 0), fmt(n_total, 0),
  est_ci(tot$share, map_tot[["share"]], 3), fmt(n_in / n_total, 3),
  est_ci(post$R_C_eff, map_row$R_C_eff), est_ci(post$p_a, map_row$p_a), rho_txt,
  s_C0, s_H0,
  est_ci(post$kappa, map_row$kappa), p_i_fixed))
```

Coverage of the 95% predictive interval. With 80 observations it should be near
0.95; much less means the model is overconfident, much more means `phi` has
grown to absorb misfit.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
obs_d |>
  left_join(band |> select(week, lo95, hi95), by = c("t_week" = "week")) |>
  summarise(coverage_95 = mean(total >= lo95 & total <= hi95))
```

## Force of infection

```{r}
set.seed(20260922)
n_draws <- 1000       # 200 is enough while adjusting the layout

## own names for the theme and the date axis of these figures, so theme_thesis
## and date_axis of the calibration figure stay as Part 1 set them
theme_plain <- theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        legend.title     = element_blank())

narrow <- theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 8))   # three panels in a row

date_axis_6m <- list(
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "6 months", date_labels = "%b\n%Y"),
  coord_cartesian(xlim = range(obs$week))
)

setting_col <- c(Hospital = "#BC3C29", Community = "#0072B5")
kappa_col   <- "#E18727"
prev_col    <- "#7876B1"   # infectious prevalence ratio, in panels A and D

x_right <- max(obs$week)   # labels end here, inside the visible range

## ---- simulate each posterior draw -------------------------------------------
par_of <- function(d) {
  c(setNames(as.numeric(d[par_names]), par_names), p_i = p_i_fixed)
}

## model day t is the date t0_date + 7 + t: wk2date() labels model week w with
## t0_date + 7 * w, the Monday that starts it, and week 1 starts on day 0
trajectory <- function(par, days = n_weeks * 7) {
  sol <- solve_model(par, 0:days)
  if (is.null(sol)) return(NULL)
  beta_C <- par[["beta_C"]]
  beta_H <- par[["kappa"]] * beta_C
  as.data.frame(sol) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(
      date     = t0_date + 7 + time,
      prev_C   = (I_C_pre + I_C_post) / (S_C + E_C + I_C_pre + I_C_post + R_C),
      prev_H   = (I_H_pre + I_H_post) / (S_H + E_H + I_H_pre + I_H_post + R_H),
      s_C      = S_C / (S_C + E_C + I_C_pre + I_C_post + R_C),
      s_H      = S_H / (S_H + E_H + I_H_pre + I_H_post + R_H),
      lambda_C = beta_C * prev_C,
      lambda_H = beta_H * prev_H
    )
}

traj <- post |>
  slice_sample(n = n_draws) |>
  mutate(draw = row_number()) |>
  group_split(draw) |>
  map_dfr(function(d) {
    s <- trajectory(par_of(d))
    if (is.null(s)) return(NULL)
    s |> mutate(draw = d$draw, kappa = d$kappa, beta_C = d$beta_C)
  })

## dates on which the outbreak is under way (median community prevalence above
## 1 in 100,000); ratios of near-zero prevalences are not meaningful
window <- traj |>
  group_by(date) |>
  summarise(p = median(prev_C), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(p > 1e-5) |>
  pull(date)

## each draw at its own peak of community prevalence, for the 95% CrI of kappa
## in A and of every ratio in D
peaks <- traj |>
  group_by(draw) |>
  slice_max(prev_C, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()

## the MAP parameter set (Posterior section): its trajectory gives every line
## and point in the figure; the draws give the 95% CrI around them
traj_map <- trajectory(par_of(map_row)) |>
  mutate(kappa = map_row$kappa)

peak_map  <- traj_map |> slice_max(prev_C, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
peak_date <- peak_map$date

## ---- A: the result ------------------------------------------------------------
## the force of infection ratio is the product of the two other ratios in the
## panel: lambda_H / lambda_C = kappa x P, with P the infectious prevalence ratio
ratio_t <- traj |>                                  # 95% CrI, day by day
  filter(date %in% window) |>
  mutate(foi  = lambda_H / lambda_C,
         prev = prev_H / prev_C) |>
  pivot_longer(c(foi, prev), names_to = "ratio") |>
  group_by(ratio, date) |>
  summarise(lo = quantile(value, 0.025),
            hi = quantile(value, 0.975), .groups = "drop")

ratio_map <- traj_map |>                            # the MAP lines
  filter(date %in% window) |>
  transmute(date,
            foi  = lambda_H / lambda_C,
            prev = prev_H / prev_C) |>
  pivot_longer(-date, names_to = "ratio", values_to = "map")

## kappa: the MAP value, with the 95% CrI of the draws
kq <- c(quantile(peaks$kappa, 0.025), map_row$kappa, quantile(peaks$kappa, 0.975))

## where each line ends, to place its label
end_y <- ratio_map |>
  filter(date <= x_right) |>
  group_by(ratio) |>
  slice_max(date, n = 1) |>
  select(ratio, map) |>
  deframe()

## Each label goes on the side of its line with more room. On the log scale, the
## room above the kappa x P line (up to P) and above the kappa line (up to 1) is a
## factor of 1 / kappa. The room below is a factor of kappa x P (down to 1) and of
## kappa / its 2.5% quantile (down to the bottom of its band).
vj <- function(above) if (above) -0.3 else 1.3
vj_foi   <- vj(1 / kq[[2]] > end_y[["foi"]])
vj_kappa <- vj(1 / kq[[2]] > kq[[2]] / kq[[1]])

pA <- ggplot(mapping = aes(date)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = peak_date, linetype = "dotted") +
  annotate("rect", xmin = min(window), xmax = max(window),
           ymin = kq[[1]], ymax = kq[[3]], fill = kappa_col, alpha = 0.25) +
  annotate("segment", x = min(window), xend = max(window),
           y = kq[[2]], yend = kq[[2]], colour = kappa_col, linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_ribbon(data = ratio_t, aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi, fill = ratio), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(data = ratio_map, aes(y = map, colour = ratio), linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(foi = "grey40", prev = prev_col), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(foi = "black", prev = prev_col), guide = "none") +
  annotate("text", x = x_right, y = end_y[["prev"]], label = "Prevalence",
           colour = prev_col, hjust = 1, vjust = -0.3, size = 2.8) +
  annotate("text", x = x_right, y = end_y[["foi"]], label = "FOI",
           hjust = 1, vjust = vj_foi, size = 2.8) +
  annotate("text", x = x_right, y = kq[[2]], label = "Ratio \u03ba",
           colour = kappa_col, hjust = 1, vjust = vj_kappa, size = 2.8) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE),
                expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.15))) +   # room for the top label
  date_axis_6m +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Hospital / community") +
  theme_plain +
  narrow

## ---- B and C: the two settings side by side ---------------------------------
## B is prevalence (a component), C the force of infection (the product), in the
## same order as panel D
long <- traj |>
  filter(date %in% window) |>
  transmute(draw, date,
            foi_Community  = 1000 * lambda_C, foi_Hospital  = 1000 * lambda_H,
            prev_Community = 1000 * prev_C,   prev_Hospital = 1000 * prev_H) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(draw, date), names_to = c("quantity", "setting"),
               names_sep = "_") |>
  group_by(quantity, setting, date) |>
  summarise(lo = quantile(value, 0.025),
            hi = quantile(value, 0.975), .groups = "drop")

long_map <- traj_map |>
  filter(date %in% window) |>
  transmute(date,
            foi_Community  = 1000 * lambda_C, foi_Hospital  = 1000 * lambda_H,
            prev_Community = 1000 * prev_C,   prev_Hospital = 1000 * prev_H) |>
  pivot_longer(-date, names_to = c("quantity", "setting"), names_sep = "_",
               values_to = "map")

## one shared legend for B and C (collected in the assembly below)
time_panel <- function(q, ylab) {
  ggplot(mapping = aes(date, colour = setting, fill = setting)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = peak_date, linetype = "dotted") +
    geom_ribbon(data = filter(long, quantity == q),
                aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25, colour = NA) +
    geom_line(data = filter(long_map, quantity == q),
              aes(y = map), linewidth = 0.6) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = setting_col) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = setting_col) +
    scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
    date_axis_6m +
    labs(x = NULL, y = ylab) +
    theme_plain +
    narrow
}

pB <- time_panel("prev", "Prevalence\nper 1,000")
pC <- time_panel("foi",  "Force of infection\n(per 1,000 per day)")

## ---- D: how the pieces combine, at the peak ---------------------------------
## each component gets a letter, and each product shows which letters multiply.
## The products follow the argument: kappa x P is the risk to a susceptible
## child; multiplying by s gives the risk to any child in the setting.
labels_D <- c(
  kappa = "Infectious contact rate ratio, \u03ba",
  prev  = "Infectious prevalence, P",
  sus   = "Susceptible proportion, s",
  foi   = "Force of infection, \u03ba \u00d7 P",
  inc   = "Incidence, \u03ba \u00d7 P \u00d7 s"
)

ratios_D <- function(d) {
  d |>
    transmute(kappa,
              prev = prev_H / prev_C,
              sus  = s_H / s_C,
              foi  = kappa * prev,
              inc  = kappa * prev * sus) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "factor")
}

decomp <- ratios_D(peaks) |>                        # 95% CrI, each draw at its peak
  group_by(factor) |>
  summarise(lo    = quantile(value, 0.025),
            hi    = quantile(value, 0.975),
            p_gt1 = mean(value > 1), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(ratios_D(peak_map) |> rename(map = value),   # the MAP, at its peak
            by = "factor") |>
  mutate(type   = if_else(factor %in% c("kappa", "prev", "sus"),
                          "Components", "Products"),
         colour = case_when(factor == "kappa" ~ kappa_col,
                            factor == "prev"  ~ prev_col,
                            TRUE              ~ "black"),
         label  = factor(labels_D[factor], levels = rev(labels_D)))

pD <- ggplot(decomp, aes(map, label, colour = colour)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi, shape = type), fill = "white") +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(Components = 16, Products = 23), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  facet_grid(type ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Ratio hospital / community at the peak", y = NULL) +
  theme_plain +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0))

## ---- assemble -----------------------------------------------------------------
## B and C share one legend, placed in its own area above them (G) so it does
## not sit over A. free() stops the long labels in D from widening the left
## margin of A. Plots fill the design areas in alphabetical order: A, B, C, D, G.
design <- "
#GG
ABC
DDD
"

fig1 <- pA + pB + pC + free(pD) + guide_area() +
  plot_layout(design = design, guides = "collect",
              heights = c(0.12, 1, 1.2)) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
  theme(legend.position  = "top",
        legend.direction = "horizontal",
        plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12))

fig1

ggsave("figs/chap3/fig_insight_1.png", fig1, width = 16, height = 9,
       units = "cm", dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

### Value FOI

```{r}
## MAP (2.5%-97.5% quantiles across draws), with d decimal places
fmt_short <- function(x, at, d = 1) {
  f <- \(v) formatC(v, format = "f", digits = d)
  sprintf("%s (%s-%s)", f(at), f(quantile(x, 0.025)), f(quantile(x, 0.975)))
}

## dates for the ranges: the dates shown in the figure, within the observed weeks
in_obs <- \(d) d |>
  filter(date %in% window, between(date, min(obs_d$date), max(obs_d$date)))

## lowest and highest value of each ratio over those dates, and the fold change
## (highest / lowest; 1 means constant), for each draw
range_of <- \(d) d |>
  in_obs() |>
  transmute(draw, foi = lambda_H / lambda_C, prev = prev_H / prev_C) |>
  pivot_longer(-draw, names_to = "ratio") |>
  group_by(ratio, draw) |>
  summarise(lowest = min(value), highest = max(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(fold = highest / lowest)

ranges     <- range_of(traj)
ranges_map <- range_of(traj_map |> mutate(draw = 0))

ranges |>
  left_join(select(ranges_map, -draw), by = "ratio", suffix = c("", "_map")) |>
  group_by(ratio) |>
  summarise(lowest  = fmt_short(lowest,  first(lowest_map)),
            highest = fmt_short(highest, first(highest_map)),
            fold    = fmt_short(fold,    first(fold_map)))

## ---- numbers for the text -----------------------------------------------------
## Run after the figure chunk. Each value is the MAP, with the 2.5% and 97.5%
## quantiles across the posterior draws in brackets.
fmt_short <- function(x, at, d = 1) {
  f <- \(v) formatC(v, format = "f", digits = d)
  sprintf("%s (%s-%s)", f(at), f(quantile(x, 0.025)), f(quantile(x, 0.975)))
}

## at the peak of community prevalence: the MAP at its own peak, and each draw
## at its own peak for the interval, as in panel D
at_peak <- \(f, d = 1) fmt_short(f(peaks), f(peak_map), d)

## over the outbreak (the dates in panel A, within the observed weeks): each
## ratio's highest / lowest value (1 means constant), per draw and for the MAP
range_of <- \(d) d |>
  filter(date %in% window, between(date, min(obs_d$date), max(obs_d$date))) |>
  transmute(draw, foi = lambda_H / lambda_C, prev = prev_H / prev_C) |>
  pivot_longer(-draw, names_to = "ratio") |>
  group_by(ratio, draw) |>
  summarise(fold = max(value) / min(value), .groups = "drop")

ranges     <- range_of(traj)
ranges_map <- range_of(traj_map |> mutate(draw = 0))
over_outbreak <- \(r) fmt_short(filter(ranges, ratio == r)$fold,
                                filter(ranges_map, ratio == r)$fold, d = 2)

## peak date: the MAP, and the 2.5% and 97.5% quantiles across draws
peak_dates <- quantile(peaks$date, c(0.025, 0.975), type = 1)

tibble(
  quantity = c(
    "Peak date, MAP (2.5% to 97.5%)",
    "Infectious prevalence at the peak, hospital (per 1,000)",
    "Infectious prevalence at the peak, community (per 1,000)",
    "FOI at the peak, hospital (per 1,000 per day)",
    "FOI at the peak, community (per 1,000 per day)",
    "FOI ratio, highest / lowest over the outbreak",
    "Prevalence ratio, highest / lowest over the outbreak",
    "Infectious contact rate ratio, kappa",
    "Infectious prevalence ratio at the peak, P",
    "Susceptible proportion ratio at the peak, s",
    "FOI ratio at the peak, kappa x P",
    "Pr(FOI ratio > 1) at the peak (%)",
    "Incidence ratio at the peak, kappa x P x s"
  ),
  value = c(
    sprintf("%s (%s to %s)", peak_map$date, peak_dates[[1]], peak_dates[[2]]),
    at_peak(\(x) 1000 * x$prev_H),
    at_peak(\(x) 1000 * x$prev_C),
    at_peak(\(x) 1000 * x$lambda_H),
    at_peak(\(x) 1000 * x$lambda_C),
    over_outbreak("foi"),
    over_outbreak("prev"),
    at_peak(\(x) x$kappa, d = 2),
    at_peak(\(x) x$prev_H / x$prev_C),
    at_peak(\(x) x$s_H / x$s_C),
    at_peak(\(x) x$kappa * x$prev_H / x$prev_C),
    sprintf("%.1f", 100 * mean(peaks$kappa * peaks$prev_H / peaks$prev_C > 1)),
    at_peak(\(x) x$kappa * x$prev_H / x$prev_C * x$s_H / x$s_C)
  )
) |>
  print(n = Inf, width = Inf)
```

## R0H

The simulation set everyone in the population susceptible, and introduce 1 infectious in the pre-rash state in the community (to check R0C), or hospital (to check R0H).

```{r}
## ---- closed forms from the next-generation matrix ----------------------------
r0h_formula <- function(beta_H,
                        eta,
                        gamma,
                        delta,
                        xi_alpha,
                        p_a,
                        p_i) {
  k <- eta + xi_alpha + delta
  beta_H * ((eta + xi_alpha) / (eta * k) +
              (1 - p_i) / gamma * (eta + xi_alpha + p_a * delta) / k)
}

r0c_formula <- function(beta_C, eta, gamma, delta, xi_alpha, p_a) {
  k <- eta + xi_alpha + delta
  beta_C * (eta + delta) / k * (1 / eta + (1 - p_a) / gamma)
}

## ---- the same quantities from the model ODE -----------------------------------
## seed_in: compartment of the index child ("I_H_pre" or "I_C_pre")
## count:   which infections to count ("cum_noso" or "cum_inf_C")
## Everyone is susceptible, so S_C = N_C and S_H = N_H at the start.
simulate_new_infections <- function(beta_C,
                                    beta_H,
                                    eta,
                                    gamma,
                                    delta,
                                    xi_alpha,
                                    p_a,
                                    p_i,
                                    N_C,
                                    N_H,
                                    seed_in,
                                    count) {
  y0 <- c(
    S_C = N_C,
    E_C = 0,
    I_C_pre = 0,
    I_C_post = 0,
    R_C = 0,
    S_H = N_H,
    E_H = 0,
    I_H_pre = 0,
    I_H_post = 0,
    Q = 0,
    R_H = 0,
    cum_onset_C = 0,
    cum_onset_H = 0,
    cum_noso = 0,
    cum_adm_rash = 0,
    cum_inf_C = 0
  )[state_names]
  y0[seed_in] <- 1   # one infectious child
  
  p <- c(
    beta_C = beta_C,
    beta_H = beta_H,
    xi_alpha = xi_alpha,
    alpha = 0,
    p_a = p_a,
    p_i = p_i,
    sigma = 0,
    eta = eta,
    gamma = gamma,
    delta = delta,
    delta_M = 1 / 7
  )
  
  ## long enough for the index child to finish its infectious period
  t_end <- 50 / min(eta, gamma)
  
  out <- ode(y0,
             c(0, t_end),
             measles_ode,
             p,
             rtol = 1e-10,
             atol = 1e-10)
  out[2, count]
}

## ---- parameter sets -------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. the baseline values
baseline <- tibble(
  beta_C = 15 / 8,
  beta_H = 15 / 8,
  eta = 1 / 4,
  gamma = 1 / 4,
  delta = 1 / 5.2,
  xi_alpha = 0.001,
  p_a = 0.3,
  p_i = 0.9
)

## 2. the baseline with p_a and p_i at their limits (0 or 1)
edges <- baseline |>
  select(-p_a, -p_i) |>
  expand_grid(p_a = c(0, 1), p_i = c(0, 1))

## 3. random values over wide ranges
set.seed(2026)
n_random <- 200
random <- tibble(
  beta_C   = runif(n_random, 0.5, 5),
  beta_H   = runif(n_random, 0.1, 10),
  eta      = 1 / runif(n_random, 1, 7),
  # pre-rash infectious period, 1 to 7 days
  gamma    = 1 / runif(n_random, 1, 7),
  # post-rash infectious period, 1 to 7 days
  delta    = 1 / runif(n_random, 1, 30),
  # length of stay, 1 to 30 days
  xi_alpha = runif(n_random, 0.001, 0.01),
  p_a      = runif(n_random),
  p_i      = runif(n_random)
)

## population sizes
## N_C is very large, so that the infections caused by one child do not reduce
## the susceptible proportion. R_0H and R_0C do not depend on N_C or N_H.
## N_H = adm * los, with adm = xi_alpha * N_C admissions per day and
## los = 1 / delta. This makes admissions equal discharges, so the population
## sizes stay constant. xi_alpha must be above 0, otherwise N_H = 0.
pars <- bind_rows(
  baseline = baseline,
  edges = edges,
  random = random,
  .id = "set"
) |>
  mutate(N_C = 1e6, N_H = xi_alpha * N_C / delta)

## ---- compare -------------------------------------------------------------------
## pick() passes each row's parameters to simulate_new_infections() by name
check <- pars |>
  mutate(
    R0H_formula   = r0h_formula(beta_H, eta, gamma, delta, xi_alpha, p_a, p_i),
    R0H_simulated = pmap_dbl(
      pick(beta_C:N_H),
      simulate_new_infections,
      seed_in = "I_H_pre",
      count = "cum_noso"
    ),
    R0C_formula   = r0c_formula(beta_C, eta, gamma, delta, xi_alpha, p_a),
    R0C_simulated = pmap_dbl(
      pick(beta_C:N_H),
      simulate_new_infections,
      seed_in = "I_C_pre",
      count = "cum_inf_C"
    )
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    starts_with("R0"),
    names_to = c("quantity", ".value"),
    names_sep = "_"
  ) |>
  mutate(rel_diff = simulated / formula - 1)

## the baseline and the four limit cases
check |>
  filter(set != "random") |>
  select(quantity, set, p_a, p_i, formula, simulated, rel_diff) |>
  arrange(quantity)

## all parameter sets
check |>
  group_by(quantity) |>
  summarise(
    n_sets = n(),
    min_value = min(formula),
    max_value = max(formula),
    max_abs_rel_diff = max(abs(rel_diff))
  )

## ---- figure ----------------------------------------------------------------------
plot_check <- function(data, title) {
  ggplot(data, aes(formula, simulated)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1,
                intercept = 0,
                colour = "grey60") +
    geom_point(size = 1.5) +
    scale_x_log10() +
    scale_y_log10() +
    labs(title = title, x = "Closed form", y = "Model simulations") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11)
}

fig_r0_check <- plot_check(filter(check, quantity == "R0H"), expression("R"[0 *
                                                                              H])) +
  plot_check(filter(check, quantity == "R0C"), expression("R"[0 * C])) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12))

fig_r0_check

# ggsave("figs/fig_r0_check.png", fig_r0_check, width = 5, height = 3, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

## Sensitivity analysis

### R0H parameters

```{r}
## =============================================================================
## Sensitivity of R_0H to beta_H, delta, p_a and p_i
## (eta, gamma and xi_alpha are fixed at their baseline values)
##
## Panel A, slope: the elasticity of R_0H with respect to each parameter, that
##   is, the % change in R_0H for a 1% increase in the parameter, with the
##   others at their baseline values. It equals the partial derivative times
##   (parameter value / R_0H). This removes the units, so the slopes of all
##   parameters are on the same scale.
## Panel B, range: R_0H as each parameter moves across its range, with the
##   others at their baseline values. The point is R_0H at the baseline values,
##   and the labels give the parameter value at each end of the bar.
## =============================================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)

## ---- R_0H and its partial derivatives ------------------------------------------
r0h <- function(beta_H, eta, gamma, delta, xi_alpha, p_a, p_i) {
  beta_H * ((eta + xi_alpha) / (eta * (eta + xi_alpha + delta)) +
              (1 - p_i) / gamma * (eta + xi_alpha + p_a * delta) / (eta + xi_alpha + delta))
}

r0h_slope <- function(par, beta_H, eta, gamma, delta, xi_alpha, p_a, p_i) {
  switch(par,
    beta_H = (eta + xi_alpha) / (eta * (eta + xi_alpha + delta)) +
               (1 - p_i) / gamma * (eta + xi_alpha + p_a * delta) / (eta + xi_alpha + delta),
    delta  = -beta_H * (eta + xi_alpha) / (eta + xi_alpha + delta)^2 *
               (1 / eta + (1 - p_i) * (1 - p_a) / gamma),
    p_a    = beta_H * (1 - p_i) * delta / (gamma * (eta + xi_alpha + delta)),
    p_i    = -beta_H * (eta + xi_alpha + p_a * delta) / (gamma * (eta + xi_alpha + delta))
  )
}

## ---- baseline values -----------------------------------------------------------
## beta_C, kappa and p_a: the MAP column of the posterior summary
base <- list(
  beta_H   = 0.612 * 2.573,   # kappa * beta_C
  eta      = 1 / 4,           # pre-rash -> post-rash
  gamma    = 1 / 4,           # post-rash -> removed
  delta    = 1 / 5.2,         # TO CONFIRM: mean length of stay 5.2 days
  xi_alpha = 0.001289992,     # fixed: setting alpha to 0 lowers R_0H by only 0.2%
  p_a      = 0.512,
  p_i      = 0.9              # assumption
)
R0H_base <- do.call(r0h, base)

## ---- range for each parameter (theoretical) ------------------------------------
## p_a, p_i: the full range of a probability, 0 to 1
## delta:    length of stay from 2 days to 30 days, so delta from 1/30 to 1/2
## beta_H:   no natural limits, so the 95% credible interval of kappa, times the
##           MAP of beta_C (with posterior draws, use the 2.5% and 97.5% quantiles
##           of kappa * beta_C)
## label_low, label_high: the parameter value printed at each end of the bar
pars <- tribble(
  ~par,     ~name,                     ~sym,      ~low,          ~high,         ~label_low,    ~label_high,
  "beta_H", "Transmission rate",       "beta[H]", 0.067 * 2.573, 0.842 * 2.573, "0.17",        "2.17",
  "delta",  "Discharge rate",          "delta",   1 / 30,        1 / 2,         "30-day stay", "2-day stay",
  "p_a",    "Admission at rash onset", "p[a]",    0,             1,             "0",           "1",
  "p_i",    "Isolation",               "p[i]",    0,             1,             "0",           "1"
)

## ---- slope and range for each parameter ----------------------------------------
## R_0H changes in one direction across each range, so its lowest and highest
## values are at the two ends
pars <- pars |>
  mutate(base_value = map_dbl(par, \(p) base[[p]]),
         slope      = map_dbl(par, \(p) do.call(r0h_slope, c(list(par = p), base))),
         elasticity = slope * base_value / R0H_base,
         R0H_low    = map2_dbl(par, low,  \(p, v) do.call(r0h, replace(base, p, v))),
         R0H_high   = map2_dbl(par, high, \(p, v) do.call(r0h, replace(base, p, v))),
         R0H_min    = pmin(R0H_low, R0H_high),
         R0H_max    = pmax(R0H_low, R0H_high),
         label_min  = if_else(R0H_low < R0H_high, label_low, label_high),
         label_max  = if_else(R0H_low < R0H_high, label_high, label_low),
         change     = R0H_max - R0H_min,
         ## exact % change in R_0H for a 10% increase in the parameter
         pct_10     = map2_dbl(par, base_value * 1.1,
                               \(p, v) 100 * (do.call(r0h, replace(base, p, v)) / R0H_base - 1))) |>
  arrange(change) |>                                  # largest at the top of the plot
  mutate(row = fct_inorder(paste0("'", name, ", '*", sym)))

## check: each elasticity against a numerical one, from R_0H at x * (1 +/- 1e-6)
elasticity_numeric <- function(p, h = 1e-6) {
  up   <- do.call(r0h, replace(base, p, base[[p]] * (1 + h)))
  down <- do.call(r0h, replace(base, p, base[[p]] * (1 - h)))
  (up - down) / (2 * h * R0H_base)
}
stopifnot(all(abs(map_dbl(pars$par, elasticity_numeric) - pars$elasticity) < 1e-6))

## numbers for the text and the table
pars |>
  select(par, base_value, slope, elasticity, pct_10, R0H_min, R0H_max, change) |>
  arrange(desc(change)) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)))
cat("R_0H at baseline:", round(R0H_base, 2), "\n")

## ---- figure ------------------------------------------------------------------------
blue  <- "#1F4E79"
minus <- \(x) str_replace(x, "^-", "\u2212")   # typographic minus sign

theme_r0h <- theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

## panel A: slope (elasticity) of R_0H with respect to each parameter
p_slope <- ggplot(pars, aes(x = elasticity, y = row)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_col(width = 0.45, fill = blue) +
  geom_text(aes(label = minus(sprintf("%.2f", elasticity)),
                hjust = if_else(elasticity >= 0, -0.25, 1.25)),
            colour = "grey20", size = 3.1) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = \(x) parse(text = x), expand = expansion(add = c(0.5, 0.7))) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1.55, 1.55), breaks = seq(-1, 1, 0.5),
                     labels = \(x) minus(as.character(x))) +
  labs(x = expression("% change in " * R[0 * H] * " per 1% increase"), y = NULL) +
  theme_r0h

## panel B: R_0H across each parameter's range
p_range <- ggplot(pars, aes(y = row)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = R0H_min, xmax = R0H_max), orientation = "y",
                width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.8, colour = blue) +
  geom_point(aes(x = R0H_base), size = 2.6, colour = blue) +
  geom_text(aes(x = R0H_min - 0.12, label = label_min), hjust = 1, colour = "grey30", size = 2.9) +
  geom_text(aes(x = R0H_max + 0.12, label = label_max), hjust = 0, colour = "grey30", size = 2.9) +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = Inf, label = "R[0*H] == 1", parse = TRUE,
           hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.4, colour = "grey30", size = 2.9) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.5, 0.7))) +   # same as panel A, so rows align
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:9, expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.1))) +
  expand_limits(x = 0) +
  labs(x = expression(R[0 * H]), y = NULL) +
  theme_r0h +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank())

p <- p_slope + p_range +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1, 2)) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
p
ggsave("figs/chap3/r0h_effect_plot.png", p, width = 9, height = 2, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

### No hospital

```{r}
beta_C <- map_row$beta_C
p_a    <- map_row$p_a

s_C0_obs <- s_C0   # the fitted model's s_C0: the framed row

## hospital susceptibility for a given community susceptibility and xi, and xi
## for a given s_C0 and s_H0 (the inverse)
s_H_from <- function(s_C0, xi) xi * s_C0 / (1 - s_C0 + xi * s_C0)
xi_from  <- function(s_C0, s_H0) s_H0 * (1 - s_C0) / (s_C0 * (1 - s_H0))

## admission rates of immune (alpha) and susceptible (xi * alpha) children:
##   alpha = alpha_bar / (1 + s_C0 * (xi - 1))
admission <- function(s_C0, xi) {
  alpha <- alpha_bar / (1 + s_C0 * (xi - 1))
  c(alpha = alpha, xi_alpha = xi * alpha)
}

## ---- one run -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## fade-out: fewer than 0.1 latent or infectious children. Isolated children
## (Q) do not transmit, so they are not counted.
gone <- function(t, y, p) {
  sum(y[c("E_C", "I_C_pre", "I_C_post", "E_H", "I_H_pre", "I_H_post")]) - 0.1
}

## infections caused by one imported case (total), and the day of fade-out
## (t_fade: NA when the threshold is not reached within max_days, 50 years).
## counters = TRUE returns the final counters instead: infections acquired in
## the community (cum_inf_C) and in hospital (cum_noso), rash onsets and
## admissions with rash.
infections <- function(s_C0, xi, kappa, p_i, los, hospital = TRUE,
                       max_days = 365 * 50, counters = FALSE) {
  delta <- 1 / los
  N_H   <- alpha_bar * N / (delta + alpha_bar)   # inpatients that balance admissions and discharges
  s_H0  <- s_H_from(s_C0, xi)
  adm   <- admission(s_C0, xi)
  
  N_h <- if (hospital) N_H else 0
  N_c <- N - N_h
  s_c <- if (hospital) s_C0 else (s_C0 * (N - N_H) + s_H0 * N_H) / N   # inpatients join the community
  
  y0 <- c(S_C = s_c * N_c - 1, E_C = 1, I_C_pre = 0, I_C_post = 0,
          R_C = (1 - s_c) * N_c,
          S_H = s_H0 * N_h, E_H = 0, I_H_pre = 0, I_H_post = 0, Q = 0,
          R_H = (1 - s_H0) * N_h,
          cum_onset_C = 0, cum_onset_H = 0, cum_noso = 0, cum_adm_rash = 0,
          cum_inf_C = 0)[state_names]
  
  p <- c(beta_C   = beta_C,
         beta_H   = if (hospital) kappa * beta_C else 0,
         xi_alpha = if (hospital) adm[["xi_alpha"]] else 0,
         alpha    = if (hospital) adm[["alpha"]] else 0,
         p_a      = if (hospital) p_a else 0,
         delta    = if (hospital) delta else 0,
         p_i = p_i, delta_M = delta_M,
         sigma = sigma, eta = eta, gamma = gamma)
  
  out <- ode(y0, c(0, max_days), measles_ode, p, rootfunc = gone,
             atol = 1e-6, rtol = 1e-8)
  end <- out[nrow(out), ]
  if (counters) return(end[c("cum_inf_C", "cum_noso", "cum_onset_C", "cum_onset_H", "cum_adm_rash")])
  troot <- attr(out, "troot")   # the time of the root; NULL if none was found
  c(total  = end[["cum_inf_C"]] + end[["cum_noso"]],
    t_fade = if (length(troot) > 0) troot[[1]] else NA)
}

## ---- runs (about 5 minutes) --------------------------------------------------------------
## mean length of stay 5.2 days. s_H0 is set directly, and xi follows from s_C0
## and s_H0. The columns of the figure are five values of kappa.
los_fix    <- 5.2
kappa_cols <- c(0.3, map_row$kappa, 1, 1.25, 1.5)

## without the hospital, isolation and kappa do not matter, but s_H0 does a
## little: the inpatients join the community
panels_sH <- expand_grid(s_C0 = seq(0.03, 0.08, by = 0.01),
                         s_H0 = seq(0, 0.75, by = 0.025)) |>
  mutate(xi  = xi_from(s_C0, s_H0),
         run = pmap(list(s_C0, xi, kappa = 0, p_i = 0, los = los_fix, hospital = FALSE),
                    infections)) |>
  unnest_wider(run) |>
  rename(none = total, t_fade_none = t_fade)

# heat_sH <- panels_sH |>
#   expand_grid(p_i = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1), kappa = kappa_cols) |>
#   mutate(run = pmap(list(s_C0, xi, kappa, p_i, los = los_fix), infections)) |>
#   unnest_wider(run) |>
#   rename(full = total, t_fade_full = t_fade) |>
#   mutate(faded   = !is.na(t_fade_none) & !is.na(t_fade_full),   # both runs faded out
#          net_pct = 100 * (full / none - 1))

# saveRDS(heat_sH, "data/heat_sH.rds")      # to redraw without rerunning
heat_sH <- readRDS("data/heat_sH.rds")

## ---- fade-out check ------------------------------------------------------------------------
heat_sH |>
  summarise(runs          = n(),
            not_faded     = sum(!faded),
            longest_years = max(t_fade_full, t_fade_none, na.rm = TRUE) / 365)

## TRUE: leave out the cells in which either run did not fade out
exclude_not_faded <- TRUE

## ---- figure ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## an outbreak means at least this many infections
outbreak_size <- 10

## colours from the GSEA palette (ggsci), eight steps from blue to red. The six
## middle steps are the bands for the change in infections; the two ends, made
## darker, are an outbreak in only one of the two scenarios.
gsea <- pal_gsea("default", n = 8)
if (is.function(gsea)) gsea <- gsea(8)   # ggsci 3 returns a palette function
darken <- \(x, f = 0.55) rgb(t(col2rgb(x) * f), maxColorValue = 255)

pct_col <- setNames(gsea[2:7], c("-100 to -50%", "-50 to -20%", "-20 to 0%",
                                 "0 to 20%", "20 to 50%", "more than 50%"))
brk_net <- c(-100, -50, -20, 0, 20, 50, Inf)

status_col <- c("Only without hospital" = darken(gsea[1]),
                "Only with hospital"    = darken(gsea[8]),
                "Neither"               = "#D9D0D6")   # mauve grey, between the blue and red ends

kappa_lab <- c("kappa == 0.3", sprintf("kappa == %.2f", kappa_cols[2]),
               "kappa == 1", "kappa == 1.25", "kappa == 1.5")
row_lab   <- \(s) sprintf("s[C0] == '%.2f'", s)

d <- heat_sH |>
  filter(faded | !exclude_not_faded) |>
  mutate(col = factor(kappa, kappa_cols, kappa_lab),
         row = row_lab(s_C0))
out_without <- filter(d, none >= outbreak_size)   # cells with an outbreak without the hospital
no_without  <- filter(d, none <  outbreak_size)   # cells without one

## reference lines in every panel: s_H0 = s_C0 (no excess susceptibility in
## hospital, dotted) and the s_H0 of the fitted xi (dashed). The point marks
## the fitted isolation, in the column of the fitted kappa.
refs   <- distinct(d, s_C0, row) |> mutate(s_H0_fit = s_H_from(s_C0, xi))
fit_pt <- refs |> mutate(col = factor(kappa_lab[2], kappa_lab), p_i = p_i_fixed)

## frames around the panels of the observed s_C0 (a row) and of the fitted
## kappa (a column)
frame_row <- tibble(row = row_lab(s_C0_obs))
frame_col <- tibble(col = factor(kappa_lab[2], kappa_lab))

## "Zero contours were generated" warnings, each followed by a min and a max
## warning, are expected: some panels have no area of that kind
fig_sH <- ggplot(mapping = aes(p_i, s_H0)) +
  ## the percentage change, drawn on every cell and covered below where there is
  ## no outbreak without the hospital. Drawing it everywhere avoids a white gap
  ## where a panel crosses from one case to the other (none depends a little on
  ## s_H0, because the inpatients join the community).
  geom_contour_filled(data = d,
                      aes(z = net_pct, fill = after_stat(names(pct_col)[as.integer(level)])),
                      breaks = brk_net) +
  geom_contour(data = out_without, aes(z = net_pct), breaks = 0,
               colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pct_col, limits = names(pct_col),
                    name = "Change in infections with the hospital",
                    guide = guide_legend(order = 1, ncol = 2)) +
  new_scale_fill() +   # the layers below use a second fill scale (legend 2)
  ## outbreak only without the hospital
  geom_contour_filled(data = out_without,
                      aes(z = log10(full / outbreak_size),
                          fill = after_stat(names(status_col)[1])),
                      breaks = c(-10, 0)) +
  ## no outbreak without the hospital: an outbreak only with it, or in neither
  geom_contour_filled(data = no_without,
                      aes(z = log10(full / outbreak_size),
                          fill = after_stat(if_else(level_high <= 0, names(status_col)[3],
                                                    names(status_col)[2]))),
                      breaks = c(-10, 0, 10)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = status_col, limits = names(status_col),
                    name = sprintf("Outbreak (%s or more infections)",
                                   scales::comma(outbreak_size)),
                    guide = guide_legend(order = 2, ncol = 1)) +
  geom_hline(data = refs, aes(yintercept = s_C0), linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(data = refs, aes(yintercept = s_H0_fit), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(data = fit_pt, aes(y = s_H0_fit), shape = 21, fill = "white",
             size = 1.4, stroke = 0.5) +
  geom_rect(data = frame_row, xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_rect(data = frame_col, xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_grid(row ~ col, labeller = label_parsed) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +   # the frames are drawn in full at the panel edges
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1), labels = c("0", "0.5", "1"), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75), labels = c("0", "0.25", "0.5", "0.75"),
                     expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = expression("Isolation, "*p[i]),
       y = expression("Hospital susceptible proportion, "*s[H0])) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 9) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0),
        panel.spacing.x = unit(3.5, "mm"),
        panel.spacing.y = unit(3, "mm"),

fig_sH

ggsave("figs/chap3/hospital_heatmap_sH.png", fig_sH, width = 12, height = 14.5,
       units = "cm", dpi = 300, bg = "white")

## ---- numbers for the text ---------------------------------------------------------------
## the smallest s_H0 (step 0.025) at which the hospital adds infections, by s_C0,
## kappa and isolation, and its product with kappa. Ward infections per
## infectious inpatient are proportional to kappa x s_H0, so the product should
## be similar across kappa. Inf: not up to s_H0 = 0.75.
heat_sH |>
  filter(faded | !exclude_not_faded, round(p_i, 1) %in% c(0, 0.5, 0.9),
         pmax(full, none) >= outbreak_size) |>
  group_by(s_C0, p_i, kappa) |>
  summarise(s_H0_adds = min(s_H0[full > none], Inf), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(product = kappa * s_H0_adds) |>
  print(n = Inf)

## the lowest isolation at which the hospital stops amplifying an imported case:
## it no longer adds infections (when there is an outbreak of 10 or more without
## the hospital) or no longer causes such an outbreak (when there is not).
## 0: no isolation needed; NA: amplifies even with p_i = 1.
iso_needed <- function(s_C0, s_H0, kappa) {
  xi_h   <- xi_from(s_C0, s_H0)
  none   <- infections(s_C0, xi_h, 0, 0, los_fix, hospital = FALSE)[["total"]]
  target <- if (none >= outbreak_size) none else outbreak_size
  f <- \(p) infections(s_C0, xi_h, kappa, p, los_fix)[["total"]] - target
  if (f(0) <= 0) return(0)
  if (f(1) > 0)  return(NA)
  uniroot(f, c(0, 1), tol = 0.001)$root
}

## for the s_H0 of the fitted xi (the dashed lines), by s_C0 and kappa
expand_grid(s_C0 = seq(0.03, 0.08, by = 0.01), kappa = kappa_cols) |>
  mutate(s_H0     = s_H_from(s_C0, xi),
         p_i_need = pmap_dbl(list(s_C0, s_H0, kappa), iso_needed),
         kappa    = round(kappa, 2)) |>
  select(-s_H0) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = kappa, values_from = p_i_need, names_prefix = "kappa_") |>
  mutate(across(starts_with("kappa_"), \(x) round(x, 2)))

## the same for a more susceptible hospital, for the text: s_C0 = 0.05, fitted kappa
iso_needed(0.05, 0.3, map_row$kappa)

## ---- longest time to fade-out --------------------------------------------------
## the slowest run in each scenario, with its parameter values (years)
bind_rows(
  `without hospital` = select(panels, los, s_C0, xi, t_fade = t_fade_none),
  `with hospital`    = select(heat, los, s_C0, xi, p_i, kappa, t_fade = t_fade_full),
  .id = "scenario"
) |>
  group_by(scenario) |>
  slice_max(t_fade, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  mutate(years = t_fade / 365)
```

```{r}
## ---- numbers for the rows close to elimination (s_C0 = 0.04 to 0.06) -------------
## without the hospital, every rash case stays in the community and is infectious
## for 1 / eta + 1 / gamma days, so R = s * beta_C * (1 / eta + 1 / gamma). This is
## the susceptible proportion at which R = 1:
s_threshold <- 1 / (beta_C * (1 / eta + 1 / gamma))
s_threshold

near_elim <- \(d) filter(d, round(s_C0, 2) %in% c(0.04, 0.05, 0.06))

## infections per imported case without the hospital, and the most with it, by panel
heat |>
  near_elim() |>
  group_by(los, s_C0, xi) |>
  summarise(none = first(none), max_full = max(full), .groups = "drop") |>
  print(n = Inf)

## at the fitted kappa (MAP), with isolation at 0.5 and at the fitted value
panels |>
  near_elim() |>
  select(los, s_C0, xi, none) |>
  expand_grid(p_i = c(0.5, p_i_fixed)) |>
  mutate(full  = pmap_dbl(list(s_C0, xi, map_row$kappa, p_i, los),
                          \(...) infections(...)[["total"]]),
         delta = 100 * (full / none - 1)) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

### Nosocomial infection

```{r}
## =============================================================================
## Share of infections acquired in hospital
##
## Same grid as hospital_heatmap.R, full model only. For each run from one
## imported case:
##   share = infections acquired in hospital / all infections
##         = cum_noso / (cum_inf_C + cum_noso)
## Shown only where there is an outbreak (outbreak_size or more infections).
##
## Run after hospital_heatmap.R: it uses infections(), s_H_from() and
## outbreak_size.
## =============================================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(ggnewscale)

## ---- runs (about 5 minutes) ---------------------------------------------------------------

## "Zero contours were generated" warnings, each followed by a min and a max
## warning, are expected: some panels have no area of that kind
noso_panel <- function(los_value) {
  no_lab <- sprintf("Fewer than %s infections", scales::comma(outbreak_size))
  d <- noso |>
    filter(los == los_value) |>
    mutate(col = factor(xi, c(2, xi_obs, 9),
                        c("xi == 2", sprintf("atop(xi == %.2f, '(observed)')", xi_obs), "xi == 9")),
           ## row label: s_C0, and below it s_H0 for the three xi columns
           row = sprintf("atop(s[C0] == '%.2f'%s, s[H0] == '%s')", s_C0,
                         if_else(near(s_C0, s_C0_obs), "~'(observed)'", ""),
                         map_chr(s_C0, \(s) toString(sprintf("%.2f", s_H_from(s, c(2, xi_obs, 9)))))))

  ggplot(d, aes(p_i, kappa)) +
    geom_contour_filled(aes(z = share, fill = after_stat(names(share_col)[as.integer(level)])),
                        breaks = brk_share) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = share_col, limits = names(share_col),
                      name = "Infections acquired in hospital",
                      guide = guide_legend(order = 1, nrow = 2)) +
    new_scale_fill() +   # the layer below uses a second fill scale
    ## no outbreak: log10(total / outbreak_size) is below 0
    geom_contour_filled(aes(z = log10(total / outbreak_size), fill = after_stat(no_lab)),
                        breaks = c(-10, 0)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = setNames("grey80", no_lab), name = "No outbreak",
                      guide = guide_legend(order = 2)) +
    facet_grid(row ~ col, labeller = label_parsed) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1), labels = c("0", "0.5", "1"), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, 1, 2), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(title = sprintf("Mean length of stay: %s days", los_value),
         x = expression("Isolation, "*p[i]), y = expression(kappa)) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 9) +
    theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
          strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0),
          axis.title.y = element_text(angle = 0, vjust = 0.5),
          plot.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
          panel.spacing.x = unit(3.5, "mm"),
          panel.spacing.y = unit(3, "mm"))
}
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
infected <- c("E_C", "I_C_pre", "I_C_post", "E_H", "I_H_pre", "I_H_post")

## deSolve stops the run when this function crosses zero
make_stop_condition <- function(threshold = 1) {
  function(time, y, parms, ...)
    sum(y[infected]) - threshold
}

max_days <- 10 * 365   # safety cap, in days

run_scenario <- function(beta_C,
                         kappa,
                         p_a,
                         p_i,
                         s_C0,
                         s_H0,
                         seed,
                         los,
                         adm,
                         threshold = 1,
                         ...) {
  stopifnot(seed > threshold)   # otherwise the run stops at once
  
  N_H      <- adm * los
  N_C      <- N - N_H
  xi       <- s_H0 * (1 - s_C0) / (s_C0 * (1 - s_H0))
  alpha    <- adm / N_C / (1 + s_C0 * (xi - 1))
  xi_alpha <- xi * alpha
  
  y0 <- c(
    S_C = s_C0 * N_C - seed,
    E_C = seed,
    I_C_pre = 0,
    I_C_post = 0,
    R_C = (1 - s_C0) * N_C,
    S_H = s_H0 * N_H,
    E_H = 0,
    I_H_pre = 0,
    I_H_post = 0,
    Q = 0,
    R_H = (1 - s_H0) * N_H,
    cum_onset_C = 0,
    cum_onset_H = 0,
    cum_noso = 0,
    cum_adm_rash = 0,
    cum_inf_C = 0
  )[state_names]
  
  p <- c(
    beta_C = beta_C,
    beta_H = kappa * beta_C,
    xi_alpha = xi_alpha,
    alpha = alpha,
    p_a = p_a,
    p_i = p_i,
    delta = 1 / los,
    delta_M = delta_M,
    sigma = sigma,
    eta = eta,
    gamma = gamma
  )
  
  sim <- function(p) {
    ode(
      y0,
      0:max_days,
      measles_ode,
      p,
      method = "lsoda",
      rootfunc = make_stop_condition(threshold),
      atol = 1e-3,
      rtol = 1e-6
    )
  }
  final <- function(sol, x)
    sol[nrow(sol), x]   # value at the stop time
  
  sol  <- sim(p)
  sol0 <- sim(replace(p, "beta_H", 0))
  
  noso  <- final(sol, "cum_noso")
  inf_C <- final(sol, "cum_inf_C")
  ## community infectious time from I_C_pre, as D_C in the Posterior section
  D_C   <- (eta + 1 / los) / (eta + xi_alpha + 1 / los) * (1 / eta + (1 - p_a) / gamma)

  tibble(
    t_end     = final(sol, "time"),
    faded     = max(t_end, final(sol0, "time")) < max_days,
    R_C_eff   = beta_C * s_C0 * D_C,
    noso_pct  = 100 * noso / (noso + inf_C),
    peak_prev = 1000 * max(sol[, "I_H_pre"] + sol[, "I_H_post"]) / N_H,
    inf_C     = inf_C,
    attr_C    = 100 * (inf_C - final(sol0, "cum_inf_C")) / inf_C
  )
}

## baseline: the MAP parameter set (Posterior section), with s_C0, s_H0, the
## length of stay and admissions fixed as in the Parameters section

  s_H0   = s_H0,
  seed   = map_row$seed,
  los    = 1 / delta,
  adm    = adm_per_day
)

pmap(base, run_scenario) |> list_rbind()
# Change threshold to check
pmap(base, run_scenario, threshold = 3) |> list_rbind()
```

### R_HH

```{r, eval=FALSE}
gsea <- pal_gsea("default", n = 6)(6)

## rate: ward infections per day that one infectious, non-isolated child
## spends on the ward
k_hh_parts <- function(beta_H, s_H0, los, p_i, p_a) {
  delta  <- 1 / los
  p_inf  <- sigma / (sigma + delta)       # becomes infectious before discharge
  p_rash <- p_inf * eta / (eta + delta)   # rash appears before discharge
  rate   <- beta_H * s_H0
  tibble(
    pre_rash  = rate * p_inf / (eta + delta),                   # before the rash
    post_rash = rate * p_rash * (1 - p_i) / gamma,              # rash on ward, not isolated
    readmit   = rate * (1 - p_rash) * p_a * (1 - p_i) / gamma,  # back with rash, not isolated
    K_HH      = pre_rash + post_rash + readmit
  )
}
```
